newsitem.title: FRANCE: Traxon Europe sees a million monthly messages.
newsitem.headline: Traxon Europe sees a million monthly messages.

text.p: Traxon Europe, the European arm of airfreight information system, Traxon, said it was hoping to generate one million electronic messages a month by the end of 1997.

"Last year, around eight million electronic messages were transmitted via Traxon Europe and this year our objective is to generate ten million messages," Traxon Europe's sales and marketing director, Christian Gillard, told Reuters.
He said messages fell into four main categories; space availability, timetables, status and air way bills.

"Air way bills messages, which concern the actual transport documents, currently represent around ten percent of global messages and we are looking to increase their volume by 40 percent in 1997 and have already surpassed this growth rate in the first few months of 1997," Gillard said.

The full list of Traxon's airline participants worldwide reads: Air Canada, Air France, British Airways Plc Cargolux, Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd, Emirates, Finnair, Japan Airlines Ltd, KLM Royal Dutch Airlines, Korean Airlines Ltd Lufthansa AG, Martinair, Royal Air Maroc, SAS, Singapore Airlines and Swissair.
In addition, Northwest Airlines and Federal Express Corp are linked to Traxon Asia with United Airlines set to follow shortly.
Two other airlines, Austrian Airlines and Air Malta are on the point of joining Traxon while Air India is also showing an interest, Gillard added.
Traxon is organised into two sister companies, Traxon Europe and Traxon Asia.
